definition: Shy Girl is a horror novel initially self-published in February 2025 by Mia Ballard.
details: Publishing rights for the book were acquired by Hachette Book Group, which released the book in the United Kingdom in November 2025 and planned to publish it in the United States in 2026. Its US release was cancelled and its UK release was discontinued after it faced accusations of being created with generative AI. Ballard denied having personally used AI in the book's writing, claiming that a freelance editor may have introduced AI-generated changes to the entirety of the text. She also stated that she would take legal action against the editor.

explainer.lead: Shy Girl is a horror novel by Mia Ballard, initially self-published in February 2025, whose releases were cancelled or discontinued after accusations that it was created with generative AI. Its case illustrates how AI-authorship accusations can affect publishing deals.

tiers.eli5: A scary book came out, then people said a computer might have helped write it, and the publisher pulled it from sale.
tiers.practitioner: For engineers working on AI writing tools, the case is a caution about provenance: Ballard denied personally using AI and said a freelance editor may have introduced AI-generated changes to the entire text. A pitfall is lacking clear records of which text passed through AI tools.
tiers.paperLevel: Not a technical term; the documented facts are publication in February 2025, Hachette acquiring rights, a November 2025 UK release, a planned 2026 US release that was cancelled, and a UK release discontinued after AI accusations.

explainer.example: Hachette acquired the book, released it in the UK in November 2025, then discontinued that release and cancelled the planned 2026 US publication after the accusations.
